tables.name: kinds
tables.description: The kinds of work Rosie books: the 243 trade files of fixture set v1, one row each, seeded from the compiled bundle's trade overlays (K-01 tradeOverlay: id, name, style, pattern and facts, with MC C5's fill), and each new kind of work drafted for one owner (S1-03), which gets its row when it is drafted so the business's kinds can name it at once. The kind matcher (C-130) reads the trade-file rows as data (Q-42: no model or index is chosen here). Per-flow money paths, switches and settings are kind_flows'.
tables.source: 02-contracts section 7 row K-24 ('The 243 kinds (id, name, booking type, money combos per flow, facts, switches, settings) seeded from the trade files'); FS row B09; FS section 3; SPEC-prof 3; MC R3, C5; S1-02; S1-03; Q-42

columns.name: id
columns.description: The kind's id. A trade-file kind: its profession file's id, the file name without .json, such as barber or plumber (K-01 tradeId). A drafted kind: new- and an id code makes, such as new-pack-hikes, so it never meets a trade file's id. K-23's company_kinds.kind_id holds the same ids.
columns.source: SPEC-prof 3 ('id'); K-01 v1 tradeId; FS row B09; S1-03; K-23 v1 company_kinds.kind_id

columns.name: name
columns.description: Its name, such as Barber or Plumber (the trade file's name); a drafted kind's name in the owner's words, such as Pack hikes. The kind matcher matches an owner's words against it (S1-02).
columns.source: SPEC-prof 3 ('name'); K-01 v1 tradeOverlay.trade.name; S1-02 ('Rosie matches Sam's words to the closest kinds of work'); S1-03

columns.name: style
columns.description: Its booking type as the trade file words it, such as Chair, Home visit or Drop-off (the demo shops' booking_type). Null only for a drafted kind, which has its pattern alone.
columns.source: SPEC-prof 3 ('style'); K-01 v1 tradeOverlay.trade.style; fixtures/v1/test-kit/shops (booking_type)

columns.name: pattern
columns.description: Its booking pattern, one of the 11 of FS section 3: what the customer picks and how the time is held. A drafted kind takes the closest one (S1-03).
columns.source: FS section 3 ('Eleven patterns appear in the profession files (field pattern)'); SPEC-prof 2 item 5; K-01 v1 tradeOverlay.trade.pattern; S1-03 ('It matches the work to the closest booking pattern')

columns.name: facts
columns.description: A trade-file kind's plug-in facts (pf.facts), the defaults a business's kind starts from at S1-04: insurance carries MC C5's list (video, forms, firststeps, documents). Null: no facts list, so every fact-gated branch shows (SPEC-master 5d); a drafted kind is always null here, since its facts are its draft's (new_work_draft_blocks). The business's own facts are K-23's company_kinds.pf_facts.
columns.source: MC R3 (code reads pf.facts by name); MC C5; SPEC-master 5d; K-01 v1 tradeOverlay.facts; K-23 v1 company_kinds.pf_facts

columns.name: source
columns.description: trade_file: seeded from a trade file of fixture set v1; new_work: drafted from one owner's own words and checklist (S1-03), offline until Rosie's team reviews it.
columns.source: 02-contracts row K-24 ('seeded from the trade files'; 'new work drafted for review (S1-03)'); S1-02 branch 'One isn't on the list yet'; S1-03

columns.description: The row's version: every update raises it by one, and a commit compares and sets it, so a write made from an old read is refused with the rows that changed (limit 4).

tables.name: kind_flows
tables.description: A trade-file kind's defaults in one flow (A: the customer comes to the business; B: the business goes to the customer), as the compiled bundle has them (K-01 tradeFlow): the main money path and the paths it really uses, the plug-in switches on, and the sign-up settings (arrive, cutoff) with MC C5's start values. Every trade file writes both flows (SPEC-prof 1), so each trade-file kind has two rows; a drafted kind has none until it is reviewed. A business's own values are K-23's (company_kinds switches per flow; flow_defaults for arrive and cutoff), which start from these at sign-up.
tables.source: 02-contracts row K-24 ('money combos per flow, facts, switches, settings'); SPEC-prof 1 and 3 ('money', 'Plug-in switches', 'Sign-up settings'); MC R3, C5; K-01 v1 tradeFlow, tradeMoney, tradeSettings; FS section 5 (A# / B#, arrive A / B, cutoff)

tables.name: picked_kinds
tables.description: The kinds of work an owner picked (S1-02 gives kinds): each kind named, in the order named, with the owner's own words for it and what it became: a listed kind, a new kind drafted for review (S1-03), or work Rosie does not book (S1-74), kept so Rosie's team can see it. S1-02 comes before S1-04 gives companies and S1-09 gives the business, so company_id and business_id are null until then; once set, the pick is that company's kind (K-23 company_kinds) and holds its plug-in text blocks (picked_kind_texts). S11-58 (NEW) adds a pick to a live business the same way.
tables.source: S1-02 (gives kinds); S1-03; S1-74; S1-04; S11-58; FS row B09; 02-contracts section 8 ('kinds | S1-02 | K-24: the business's kinds of work')

tables.name: picked_kind_texts
tables.description: Each business kind's plug-in text blocks (S1-11 gives pf.license to pf.edges): the 11 free-text pf keys, one row each, stored whole as the AI reads them, sub-keys guidance only. For a listed kind each block is its trade file's value as JSON text, unchanged (K-01 pluginText); for a drafted kind, the draft's. This is FS business.extras ({"<profession id>": {"pf.license": ...}}), held per pick. The typed keys (pf.facts, pf.switches, pf.settings) never come here: K-23's company_kinds and flow_defaults hold a business's own, and kinds and kind_flows the trade's.

tables.name: new_work_drafts
tables.description: A plug-in drafted for new work (S1-03): a kind of work not on Rosie's list, drafted from the owner's own words and price list through a fixed checklist of 15 blocks, offline until a person on Rosie's team reviews it within 1 business day. One per pick whose outcome is new_work; the drafted kind is that pick's kind (kinds, source new_work, with its closest booking pattern). The review itself is K-37's review_items row of kind new_work whose subject is this row; its decision is written back here as the state.
tables.source: S1-03; S1-02 branch 'One isn't on the list yet' (safe default: 'draft it as new work, offline until Rosie's team reviews it'); S11-58; 02-contracts row K-24 ('new work drafted for review (S1-03)'); K-37 v1 review_items (kind new_work, subject_table, subject_row_id)

Until approved it is offline.

tables.name: new_work_draft_blocks
tables.description: The owner's answer to one block of S1-03's checklist of 15 (1 Danger and safety words to 15 Free estimates, who collects), with the facts and switches it set, as the screen names them. Each block starts from its safe default; a block with no row is still at it, so its protective facts (contracts, crews and forms) stay on. A clear no skips the block and sets nothing; only that turns a protective fact off. Which facts the draft ends with, and the business's own copy, is code's and K-23's (company_kinds), from these rows.
tables.source: S1-03 (its form: the 15 blocks; 'Each starts from its safe default, and a no skips that block'; 'Each answer sets a switch or a fact'; 'The screen names every fact each block sets'; 'Protective facts start on: contracts, crews and forms'; 'Only the business's clear no turns a protective fact off. Silence or a skipped block keeps it on'); FS rows T13, V15, K07 (S1-03 blocks 12 and 15)
